bull.b: Extremely low leverage and a large equity base provide durable financial flexibility, lowering refinancing risk and enabling the company to fund clinical programs and strategic initiatives without immediate external pressure. This supports multi-quarter R&D execution and partnering optionality.

Robust Phase 2a efficacy and favorable safety in psoriasis materially de-risks the lead program and strengthens clinical proof-of-concept. This increases likelihood of advancement, improves partnering and licensing prospects, and underpins longer-term commercial viability in dermatology.

Clear shareholder backing for board composition and auditor provides governance stability and management mandate. Stable leadership and aligned investors reduce execution risk during multi-year clinical development and aid continuity in strategic decision-making.

bear.b: Being pre-revenue means the company has no product cash inflows and must rely on capital markets or partners to fund operations. This structural reality extends the timeline to self-sustaining profitability and keeps financing and dilution risk central to the investment thesis.

Escalating operating losses and high cash burn create persistent funding needs that can pressure liquidity planning and push the company to raise capital on dilutive terms. Sustained negative free cash flow also increases dependency on external financing or partnering to sustain late-stage development.

Imposed dosing restrictions for ORKA-001 in IBD limit the company's ability to pursue those indications or combination regimens near-term, narrowing addressable markets and complicating partnering or development strategies. These contractual limits could delay commercialization optionality for years.
